results.title: Get Started With Custom Fields
results.body:
In this article, you will learn how to begin using custom fields effectively in Clio Manage and Clio Grow. Custom fields in Clio Manage and Clio Grow allow your firm to capture additional information beyond the standard fields available for contacts and matters. Custom field sets are collections of individual custom fields grouped. You can add these field sets to a contact or matter for a specific practice area. These firm-wide definitions help you organize and track case details.

Setting up your custom fields helps ensure data consistency and efficiency. Below are some tips to help you start with custom fields:

  • Create practice area fields proactively: Define custom fields and field sets for your practice areas before you urgently need them. This ensures consistency and saves time during client intake and matter creation.
  • Plan your custom fields: Before creating fields, outline the specific information you need to track. Consider how this data will be used in documents, reports, or workflows to ensure your custom fields meet your firm's needs.

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.

Note: All users can use custom fields, but only users with administrator permissions can create, edit, or delete custom fields and custom field sets.

Custom field types in Clio Manage

When creating new custom fields, you will need to select what type of field will be used. Below is a breakdown of each “Type”:

Tip: You can use all custom field types as merge fields when creating document templates in Clio Manage. Learn more here.

Checkbox

This is a single checkbox used to record "Yes" or "No" information. Checking the box will record "Yes." Leaving the box blank will record "No." This is useful for status on filings, conflict of interest checks, and more.

Contact Select

This allows you to select a contact that already exists in your account. Once the custom field is added to a matter and a contact is selected, the contact’s name will appear hyperlinked and you can use the contact's custom fields as merge fields to generate document templates for your matter. This gives you more flexibility and eliminates the need to add a contact as a related contact.

Date

This field allows you to select a date for a custom field.

Email Address

This will prompt you to enter a valid email address for a custom field. When entered, the email address will appear hyperlinked.

Integer

This is a numerical value field for a custom field.

Matter Select

This allows you to select a matter that already exists in your account. When selected, the matter will appear hyperlinked.

Money

This will prompt you to enter a numerical value with a maximum of two decimal points. Currency characters, such as the $ symbol, are not permitted.

Picklist

This allows you to create a dropdown menu of options. Each picklist option has a 64-character limit.

Text (Multi-Line)

This allows you to enter multiple lines of text up to a maximum of 64,000 characters.

Text (One-Line)

This allows you to enter a single line of text up to a maximum of 255 characters.

Time

This will prompt you to enter a clock time format. You can use 12-hour or 24-hour time.

Web Address

This allows you to enter a website address. When entered, the website address will appear hyperlinked.

 

Custom field types in Clio Grow

When creating new custom fields, you will need to select what type of field will be used. Below is a breakdown of each “Field type”:

Checkbox

This is a single checkbox used to record "Yes" or "No" information. Checking the box will record "Yes." Leaving the box blank will record "No." This is useful for status on filings, conflict of interest checks, and more.

Contact Select

This allows you to select a contact that already exists in your account.

Date

This field allows you to select a date for a custom field.

Dropdown

This allows you to create a dropdown menu of options. Each dropdown option has a 55-character limit.

Email

This will prompt you to enter a valid email address for a custom field.

Integer

This is a numerical value field for a custom field.

Money

This will prompt you to enter a numerical value. Currency characters, such as the $ symbol, are permitted but decimal points are not.

Paragraph Text

This allows you to enter multiple lines of text up to a maximum of 64,000 characters.

Single Line Text

This allows you to enter a single line of text up to a maximum of 255 characters.

Website

This allows you to enter a website address. When entered, the website address will appear hyperlinked.

results.name: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Client reports provide a comprehensive overview of client balances, bank account and matter transaction history, non-billable and billable work in progress, and trust account balances. On matters with multiple clients, most reports apply to the default client only. The Matter balance summary, Trust management, Invoice payments, Client Ledger, and Trust Listing reports support multiple clients on a matter.

See below for a summary of each client report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.

Client activity report

The client activity report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of billed and unbilled time and expense activities across matters. This report does not include non-billable time. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

Activity type

This column shows whether the recorded activity is a time entry or expense entry.

Status

This column shows whether the activities are billed or unbilled. Activities are divided by billed and unbilled status, with billed activities appearing first with their subtotal, followed by unbilled activities.

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry.

Activity category

This column shows the activity category recorded when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Description

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses for the listed activity.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for the matter.

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for each of a client's matters.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for all of a client's matters.

 

Client ledger report

The client ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed view of client trust and operating transactions. This report also shows payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust ledger report

The trust ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of client and matter transactions and balances across all trust accounts. The report includes payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. You can use this report to submit to regulators. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Payer/Payee

This column shows information about the person making or receiving a payment. This information is useful when the payer or payee is not the client themselves.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust interest calculation report

The trust interest calculation report is designed to calculate interest earned on deposited client matter trust funds across all trust accounts. You can use this report to calculate interest for trust funds based on rate, compounding period, and date range for a specific client or matter. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the IOLTA account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists trust funds deposited into the IOLTA account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money remaining after each listed transaction.

Rate

This column lists the selected interest rate for each deposit.

Balance start date

The start date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Balance end date

The end date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Days held

This column shows the total number of days of the interest period you selected to generate the report.

Interest

This column shows the amount of interest accrued based on the balance for the selected period.

A summary of the Closing balance, Total interest, and Closing balance with interest is also provided for each calculation in the report.

If you generate this report in Clio, i.e., you generate a Web report, you have the option to post the calculated interest directly to the client funds you hold. Next to the Total interest amount calculated for the client funds held in a client funds account (per matter and client), click Apply Interest. You can change the transaction date and description for the transaction, then click Record transaction to create this ledger entry in the client funds account. The Source/Destination field for the entry will be “Trust Interest Calculation Report”.

Once you apply interest to the client funds, your subsequent Client funds interest reports will show the last five transactions where you applied interest to the account.

 

Trust management report

The trust management report is designed to give firms an overview of unbilled time and expense activities, trust account balances, and minimum trust thresholds. You can use this report to compare billable work against trust fund holdings. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of each client

Matter

This column lists the matters for each client.

Unbilled amount

This column shows the amount of unbilled time and expense entries for each matter.

Amount in trust

This column shows the amount of funds currently in trust for the client or matter.

Minimum threshold

This column lists the minimum threshold set for matter trust funds. This amount can be changed by editing the matter and changing the number for Trust balance notification under Billing preference.

Amount below minimum

This column shows the amount that a trust balance has fallen below the minimum threshold set for the matter.

 

 

Trust listing report

The trust listing report is designed to give firms a quick summary of client trust fund balances across all client accounts. This report includes an opening and closing balance summary. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Account name

This column shows the name of the trust account.

Last activity date

This column shows the most recent transaction in the client's trust account.

Client balance

This column shows the current amount in trust for the client. This balance may be different from the amount shown in the matter's Dashboard if you generate the report for a specific date range. This means that if a client had trust funds in the account before that selected date range and payments were made during the date range, the report will only pull in transactions, which will result in a negative balance.

Unlinked

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Include balances not associated with a client before running the report. It shows trust funds that are not linked to a specific client.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Work in progress report

The work in progress report is designed to give firms a detailed view of unbilled time and expense activities for matters. This report only shows activities on bills in draft, bills pending approval, and activities not on any bills. It will not show activities on any approved or paid bills. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

User

This column lists the firm user assigned on the activity entry.

Description

This column shows the activity category selected when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Note

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for each of the client's matters.

Client total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for all of the client's matters.

 

Bank account activity report

The bank account activity report is designed to give firms a detailed view of funds in and funds out across all firm bank accounts. This report also includes the account balance. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Client

This column lists the client associated with the transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered into the Description field when a payment was recorded.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

Next up

Learn more about generating reports, creating reports presets, and viewing a history of generated reports: Clio Manage Reports, Presets, and History.

results.name: Customize Grow AI
results.title: Customize Grow AI
results.body:
Before Grow AI starts working on your leads, administrators can set the firm's practice areas, specify the information to collect from each lead and the questions to ask leads, and the languages you want Grow AI to respond in. These settings apply to every Grow AI lead intake channel.

You manage all of this in Clio Grow under Settings > Grow AI.

Important: Add your intake criteria before you connect a channel. Until you do, Grow AI does not know which matters your firm takes or what to ask leads about.

 

Import your firm's details from your website

Rather than building your intake criteria from scratch, you can have Grow AI read your firm's website and suggest criteria based on what it finds.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. In the notice at the top of the page, click Import from website.
  3. Follow the prompts, then review what Grow AI suggests.

Review the imported criteria carefully and adjust anything that does not reflect the matters your firm currently takes.

 

Set your intake criteria

Your intake criteria tell Grow AI which matters your firm takes and what to collect from a lead before booking them. Grow AI screens each lead against these criteria to produce a fit assessment.

Note: Leads that do not match your criteria are not turned away. They arrive in your lead inbox marked for review, so your team can decide how to proceed.

 

Add a practice area

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click Intake criteria.
  3. Click Add practice area.
  4. Select the practice area, then click Save.

Repeat for each practice area your firm takes. To change a practice area, click the edit (pencil) icon next to it. To remove one, click the delete (bin) icon.

 

Choose the information to collect

For each practice area, you can choose what Grow AI collects from a lead during the conversation.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click Intake criteria.
  3. Click a practice area to open it.
  4. Review the fields under Information to collect. Some fields are always collected and cannot be removed:
    • Contact details: full name, email address, and phone number
    • A brief summary of the lead's situation
    • The location of the legal matter, which Grow AI uses to determine whether the lead qualifies
  5. To remove an optional field, click the delete (bin) icon next to it.
  6. To add a field, click Add field, then select a field from the list. The available fields depend on the practice area. For example, a divorce practice area offers fields such as date of marriage, date of separation, and whether children are involved.
  7. Click Save.
Tip: Collect only what you need to decide whether a lead is a good fit. Grow AI gathers these details conversationally, so a long list makes for a longer conversation and more chances for a lead to drop off.

 

Set the locations you serve

For each practice area, add the locations where your firm offers that service. Grow AI compares a lead's location against this list when assessing fit.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click Intake criteria.
  3. Click a practice area to open it.
  4. Under Locations where this service is offered, select a location. You can add up to 10 locations.
  5. Click Save.

 

Set up appointment booking

When appointment booking is on, Grow AI offers a consultation to leads whose location and practice area match your criteria and who raise no conflicts.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click Intake criteria.
  3. Click a practice area to open it.
  4. Toggle Appointment booking on.
  5. Select an Appointment type. This determines the length of the consultation and whose calendar it books into.
  6. Optional: Next to After booking, click Edit to change what happens to the lead once the consultation is booked.
  7. Click Save.
Note: Appointment types come from your Clio Scheduler settings. To add or change one, see Clio Grow Appointments and Scheduler settings.

 

Set your frequently asked questions

Grow AI answers common questions from leads using the FAQ you set here, so leads get your firm's answers rather than generic ones. Clio provides a starting set of questions and answers that you can edit, remove, or add to.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click FAQ.
  3. To edit an existing question, click the arrow next to it, update the Question or Answer, then click Save.
  4. To remove a question, click the delete (bin) icon next to it.
  5. To add a question, click Add question, enter the Question and Answer, then click Save.
  6. Click Done.

 

Set your languages

Grow AI replies to leads in the languages you select.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. Click Languages.
  3. Select a Primary language. Grow AI uses this for the first message in a conversation, and for any lead whose language you have not added.
  4. Optional: Under Additional languages, add any other languages you want to support. Leads who write in one of these languages get a reply in the same language.
  5. Click Save.

 

Test how Grow AI responds

Before you connect a channel, you can hold a conversation with Grow AI as though you were a lead, to check that your criteria, questions, and booking work the way you expect.

  1. In Clio Grow, go to Settings > Grow AI.
  2. In the test panel on the right, select the Email, Phone, or Web chat tab.
  3. For email and web chat, describe a situation as a lead would and send the message.
  4. For phone, click Call now to hear the voice agent and test the conversation out loud.

Work through a realistic inquiry for each practice area you take, and check that Grow AI asks for the details you expect, answers questions the way your firm would, and offers a consultation when the lead qualifies.

 

Up next

Once Grow AI is set up for your firm, connect a channel so it can start working on real leads:

  • Grow AI's Website Chat Tool: Add the chat widget to your firm's website.
  • Set Up the Voice Agent: Forward your firm's calls to the voice agent.
  • Grow AI's Email Agent: Connect an inbox so Grow AI can reply to lead emails.

results.title: Create and Manage Custom Roles
results.body:
In Clio, custom roles enable precise control over user access to firm and client information. When creating a new custom role, you can start from scratch and edit each permission category individually or select a role to start with a set of permissions which you adjust for your specific needs or as responsibilities change. Role templates include both built-in and custom roles with built-in role templates inheriting non-configurable permissions.

Create custom roles

You can create a custom role from the Users page in Clio Admin or from the Roles and Permissions page. After you create the custom role, refer to Assign and Unassign Roles to apply these permissions to Clio users at your firm.

Roles and Permissions Clio Admin
  1. Go to Settings > Roles and Permissions.
    • The roles dashboard will open in a new tab or window
  2. Select New Role in the top right corner.
  3. Under Role details, enter a Role name and a Role description.
  4. Optional: Select an existing role as a template under Choose a role template.

  5. Use the left navigation pane to select each of the various permissions "areas" (Contacts, Matters, Financials, etc.), then use the toggles and dropdowns to configure the role's permissions. Learn more about the various permissions and what they mean in Overview of Custom Role Permissions.

    Note: Standard role templates inherit non-configurable permissions. Refer to Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage to learn about non-configurable standard role permissions.
  6. Click Create custom role.
Phased release: This feature is being released in phases and may not yet be enabled for your firm.
  1. In Clio Admin, click Roles & Permissions.
  2. Click + Custom role.
  3. Select New Role in the top right corner.
  4. Under Role details, enter a Role name and a Role description.
  5. Optional: Select an existing role as a template under Choose a role template.

  6. Use the left navigation pane to select each of the various permissions "areas" (Contacts, Matters, Financials, etc.), then use the toggles and dropdowns to configure the role's permissions. Learn more about the various permissions and what they mean in Overview of Custom Role Permissions.

    Note: Standard role templates inherit non-configurable permissions. Refer to Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage to learn about non-configurable standard role permissions.
  7. Click Create custom role.

 

Edit custom roles

Edits to custom roles are effective immediately. The user can refresh their window to see permissions updates. You can edit a custom role from the Users page in Clio Admin or from the Roles and Permissions page.

Roles and Permissions Clio Admin
  1. Go to Settings > Roles and Permissions

  2. In the Action column, click the pencil icon.

    Tip: You can also duplicate standard roles and adjust permissions as responsibilities change.

  3. Use the left navigation pane to select each of the various permissions "areas" (Contacts, Matters, Financials, etc.), then use the toggles and dropdowns to configure the role's permissions. Learn more about the various permissions and what they mean in Overview of Custom Role Permissions.

    Note: Standard role templates inherit non-configurable permissions. Refer to Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage to learn about non-configurable standard role permissions.
  4. Click Update Role.
Phased release: This feature is being released in phases and may not yet be enabled for your firm.
  1. In Clio Admin, click Roles & Permissions.
  2. In the Action column, click Edit.
  3. In the Role details section, edit the name and/or description and add or remove firm users as needed.

  4. Use the left navigation pane to select each of the various permissions "areas" (Contacts, Matters, Financials, etc.), then use the toggles and dropdowns to configure the role's permissions. Learn more about the various permissions and what they mean in Overview of Custom Role Permissions.

    Note: Standard role templates inherit non-configurable permissions. Refer to Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage to learn about non-configurable standard role permissions.
  5. Click Update Role.

 

Duplicate custom roles

If you need to create a role that is similar to another, you can duplicate it before making the needed edits. You can duplicate a custom role from the Users page in Clio Admin or from the Roles and Permissions page.

Roles and Permissions Clio Admin
  1. Go to Settings > Roles and Permissions.
  2. Click the three vertical dots next to the role name.
  3. Select Duplicate Role.
    • Update the role name and description.
  4. Use the left navigation pane to select each of the various permissions "areas" (Contacts, Matters, Financials, etc.), then use the toggles and dropdowns to configure the role's permissions. Learn more about the various permissions and what they mean in Overview of Custom Role Permissions.
  5. Note: Standard role templates inherit non-configurable permissions. Refer to Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage to learn about non-configurable standard role permissions.
  6. Click Create custom role.
Phased release: This feature is being released in phases and may not yet be enabled for your firm.
  1. In Clio Admin, click Roles &and Permissions.
  2. In the Action column, click the more icon (three vertical dots) for the role you want to duplicate.
  3. Select Duplicate.

The duplicate of the role will appear in your list as Copy of [Role name]. You can then edit the role as needed.

 

Archive custom roles

You can archive a custom role from the Users page in Clio Admin or from the Roles and Permissions page.

Roles and Permissions Clio Admin
  1. Go to Settings > Roles and Permissions.
  2. Click the three vertical dots next to the role name.
  3. Select Archive.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, select Archive.
Phased release: This feature is being released in phases and may not yet be enabled for your firm.
  1. In Clio Admin, click Roles & Permissions.
  2. In the Action column, click Edit.
  3. Click Archive.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, click Archive.

results.name: Overview of Custom Role Permissions
results.title: Overview of Custom Role Permissions
results.body:
With Clio you can create custom roles and apply specific permissions to these roles to ensure that every user in your firm has the right access to the information they need and the ability to take the necessary actions in Clio. Review the information below to understand what level of access you can control and apply when you create a custom role.

Important: When you enable a permission that depends on others, Clio enables those automatically and shows a confirmation listing what changed. Select Undo change in that message if you don't want the dependent permissions enabled.

Contacts management

Contact management permissions control a user's ability to view and manage contacts, as well as define what actions a user can perform with them.

  • Create contacts: Allows users to add a new contact, person, or company to their firm.

    Note: Enabling Create contacts will also enable the Edit contacts permission.
  • Edit contacts: Allows users to edit contact properties like type, name, contact information, address, tags, custom fields, employees, and billing preferences

  • Delete contacts: Allows users to remove a single contact record from the system. A deleted contact can be recovered by the system administrator.

    Note: Enabling Delete contacts will also enable the Edit contacts permission.

    • Bulk delete contacts: Allow users to remove multiple contacts simultaneously.

      Note: Enabling Bulk delete contacts will also enable Delete contacts.
  • Export contacts: Enables the exporting of the firm's contacts via a PDF or CSV file.
  • Send review requests: Allows users to send a review request.

 

Matter management

Matter management permissions control user access to matters and all associated information, including documents, notes, communications, and activities. You can define which roles can view, edit, create, delete, and export matter-related information. This ensures data integrity and appropriate matter access for each user role. These permissions define what a user can do with matters.

  • Create matters: Allows users to create a new matter.
  • Edit matter properties: Allow users to edit properties for a single matter.

    • Bulk edit matters: Allow users to edit multiple matters simultaneously.

      Note: Enabling Bulk edit matters will also enable the Edit matter properties permission.

  • Delete matters: Allows users to delete a matter.

    Important: Deleting a matter is a permanent action.
    Note: Enabling Delete matters will also enable the Edit matter properties permission.
    • Bulk delete matters: Allow users to delete multiple matters simultaneously.
  • Export Matters: Allow users to export matters in PDF or CSV format.
  • View matter timeline: Allow users to see a chronological view of all activities and updates related to a specific matter. This includes actions like document uploads, time entries, and stage changes, located in the matter dashboard.
  • View restricted matters: Views high-level info for matters the user cannot access.
  • View matter financials: Allow users read-only access to the financial overview section on the matter dashboard, including, work in progress balance, outstanding balance, matter trust funds balance, matter budget (Billable and Non-billable).

 

Timekeeping

Timekeeping permissions control a user's access to activities and expenses.

View Activities

  • View all activities: Allow users to view all activities.
  • View activities from accessible matters: Allow users to view all activities for matters they own or have access to.
  • View own activities: Allow users to view their own activities only.

Manage Activities

  • Manage all activities: Allow users to manage all activities.
  • View activities from accessible matters: Allow users to manage all activities for matters they own or have access to.
  • View own activities: Allow users to manage their own activities only.

 

Financial management

Financial permissions control access to bills, transactions, and accounts. These permissions are critical for custom roles as they determine a user's access to financial subtabs (e.g., Transactions and Bills) within a matter or contact card. These permissions determine a user's access to financial actions and details of your firm's finances.

 

Accounts

Accounts permission allows users to see account information based on the following three levels:

  • All bank accounts: Includes all accounts in the firm, account balances, and account properties. Enables access to accounts in the global navigation.
  • Limited: Display account names and essential details for managing transactions and bills without displaying balances. Does not enable access to accounts in the global navigation.

  • None: Does not see any account information.

    Note: Selecting None will disable the Manage bills and trust requests and View transactions permissions.

 

Transactions

  • View transactions: Allows users to see the Transactions tab within a Matter or Contact card. This permission is required for users to view trust account activity and retainer balances.

    Note: To view transactions, the user also needs at minimum the Limited view of bank account information permission for Accounts.

 

Bills and trust requests

  • View bills and trust requests: Allow users to view the Bills section in the left navigation and the Bills tab in Matters and Contacts, as well as viewing, quick viewing, downloading, and printing bills and copying links to bills.

    Granular billing permissions within this option include allowing this permission for All bills & trust requests or limiting this permission to Accessible matters or Responsible attorney. Select None to prevent the user from viewing any bills or trust requests.

  • Manage draft bills and trust requests: Allow users to edit and delete draft bills and trust requests, and submit them for approval.

    Granular billing permissions within this option include allowing this permission for All bills & trust requests or limiting this permission to Accessible matters or Responsible attorney. Select None to prevent the user from managing any draft bills or trust requests.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the same access level for View bills and trust requests.

  • Approve bills and trust requests: Allow users to approve bills and trust requests that have been submitted for approval.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable View bills and trust requests.

  • Process bills and trust requests: Allow users to void bills and trust requests, and record payments.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View bills and trust requests and View bank accounts permissions.

  • Send bills and trust requests: Allow users to send bills and trust requests to clients, and mark bills as sent.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View bills and trust requests permission.

  • Create bills and trust requests: Allow users to create new bills, new trust requests, statements of accounts, legal aid bills, quick bills, and duplicate new requests.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View activities and View bills and trust requests permissions.

 

Firm settings

Firm settings permissions control a user's ability to view and manage your firm's administrative information. These permissions define what a user can do with firm-wide settings.

  • View account firm feed: Allow users to view the firm feed via the firm's dashboard.
  • Manage roles: Allow users to create, edit, archive, assign, and unassign roles to other firm users.
  • Manage users: Allow users to invite, remove, and edit firm user information.
  • Manage custom fields: Allow users to create, edit, delete, and convert contact and matter custom fields.
  • Manage location for review requests: Allow users to manage the Google business profile selected for Client Reviews.

 

Conflict check

Conflict check settings control a user's ability to initiate conflict checks and view the conflict check report. Learn about conflict checks.

  • Manage conflict checks: Any potential conflict found that is associated with a matter to which a user does not have access will appear as a line item marked as hidden and will be inaccessible to the user.

  • View conflict check report: By default, only administrators have the ability to view a conflict check report.

    Important: When applying this permission, a user will be able to view the full PDF report. The report includes information about all conflict check results, including details that the user may not normally have access to, as specified by the matter permissions.

 

Up next

  • Create and Manage Custom Roles: Build a custom role, apply the permissions described above, and edit or delete roles as your firm's needs change.
  • Assign and Unassign Roles: Once your custom roles are set up, assign them to users in your firm.
  • Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage: If you would rather use Clio's predefined roles instead of building your own, read this article for an overview of the roles available and the access each one provides.
